steps.body: Not every equation has an answer. When you solve and the variable DISAPPEARS, leaving a FALSE statement like 3 = 5, the equation has NO solution — no value of x could ever make it true.

panels.title: Step 1
panels.body: Subtract 2x from both sides. The x-terms cancel completely.

panels.title: Step 2
panels.body: You're left with 3 = 5 — no x at all.

panels.title: Step 3
panels.body: 3 = 5 is FALSE, and no value of x can fix it — so there is NO solution.

widget.successFeedback: Exactly — when the variable cancels and leaves a false statement, there's no solution.

steps.body: This happens when both sides have the SAME x-coefficient but DIFFERENT constants — like two parallel lines that never meet. The x-terms cancel, and the leftover numbers can't be equal.

explanationVariants: 4x + 1 = 4x + 9: subtract 4x to get 1 = 9, which is false — no solution.
Same x-coefficient, different constants → the x cancels leaving a false statement → no solution.

choices.label: No solution
choices.feedback: Right — subtracting 4x leaves 1 = 9, which is false.

choices.label: One solution
choices.feedback: The x-terms cancel (both 4x), leaving 1 = 9 — false — so there's no solution, not one.

choices.label: Infinitely many
choices.feedback: That would need the leftover statement to be TRUE (like 1 = 1) — here it's 1 = 9, which is false: no solution.

choices.label: x = 8
choices.feedback: The x cancels entirely, so there's no x-value at all — the equation has no solution.

explanationVariants: Same x-coefficient (both 3x) with different constants means the x cancels and leaves a false statement — no solution.
Matching x-terms but different constants is the no-solution signature.

options.label: 3x + 7 = 3x + 2
options.feedback: Right — same 3x on both sides, different constants (7 vs 2): the x cancels, leaving 7 = 2, false.

options.label: 3x + 7 = 2x + 2
options.feedback: Different x-coefficients (3x vs 2x) — the x does NOT cancel, so this has one solution.

options.label: 3x + 7 = 3x + 7
options.feedback: Same x AND same constants — this is always true, so infinitely many solutions, not none.

options.label: 2x + 7 = 3x + 2
options.feedback: Different x-coefficients — this has one solution, not none.

explanationVariants: 3(x + 2) = 3x + 5 expands to 3x + 6 = 3x + 5; subtract 3x to get 6 = 5, false — no solution.
After distributing, same x-coefficient but 6 ≠ 5 → no solution.

choices.label: No solution
choices.feedback: Right — distribute to 3x + 6 = 3x + 5, then 6 = 5 is false.

choices.label: One solution
choices.feedback: After distributing, both sides have 3x — they cancel, leaving 6 = 5 (false), so no solution.

choices.label: Infinitely many
choices.feedback: That needs a TRUE leftover statement — here it's 6 = 5, false: no solution.

choices.label: x = 1
choices.feedback: The x cancels after distributing, so there's no x-value — no solution.

explanationVariants: For no solution, keep the x-coefficients equal but make the constants differ: 6x + 1 = 6x + 9 works (1 ≠ 9).
Match the x-terms, differ the constants → no solution.

widget.prompt: Which value of ▢ makes 6x + 1 = 6x + ▢ have NO solution?

options.label: Any number except 1 (like 9)
options.feedback: Right — matching 6x with a DIFFERENT constant makes the leftover statement false: no solution.

options.label: Just 1, and nothing else
options.feedback: ▢ = 1 makes both sides identical (6x + 1 = 6x + 1) — that's infinitely many solutions, not none.

options.label: 0 only, no other number
options.feedback: 0 works (1 ≠ 0), but so does any number except 1 — it's not the only choice.

options.label: No value ever can work
options.feedback: Many values work — any constant except 1 gives a false leftover statement and thus no solution.

hints: No solution needs the x-terms to cancel and the leftover numbers to disagree.
The x-terms already match (6x = 6x). So the constant ▢ must DIFFER from 1.
Any ▢ except 1 (such as 9) makes 1 = ▢ false, giving no solution.

steps.body: No solution: the variable cancels and leaves a false statement.
takeaways: If x vanishes and you get a false statement (like 3 = 5), there's no solution.
This happens with equal x-coefficients but different constants.
Geometrically, it's two parallel lines that never meet.

concept.body: An equation has NO solution when the variable cancels and leaves a FALSE statement (like 3 = 5). This happens with equal x-coefficients but different constants.

explanationVariants: 2x + 5 = 2x + 1: subtract 2x to get 5 = 1, false — no solution.
Same 2x, different constants → the x cancels leaving 5 = 1, false → no solution.

choices.label: No solution
choices.feedback: Right — subtracting 2x leaves 5 = 1, which is false.

choices.label: One solution
choices.feedback: The 2x terms cancel, leaving 5 = 1 (false) — so no solution, not one.

choices.label: Infinitely many
choices.feedback: That needs a true leftover statement — here 5 = 1 is false: no solution.

choices.label: x = 4
